title: DO-WHILE
objectives: Understand that DO-WHILE is a post-test loop (body first, check after)
Tell the difference between WHILE (pre-test) and DO-WHILE (post-test)

hook.text: You want to show a menu at least ONCE, no matter what the user picks. WHILE cannot guarantee that, because it checks the condition first.

concept.heading: The post-test loop
concept.body: DO-WHILE runs the body ONCE first, THEN checks the condition. If the condition is TRUE, the body runs again; if it is FALSE, the loop ends. This guarantees the body runs AT LEAST ONCE.

concept.heading: How it differs from WHILE
concept.body: WHILE checks the condition first, so if the condition is FALSE from the start, the body may never run. DO-WHILE puts the condition at the end, so the body always runs at least once. There is only one difference: the PLACE of the check (before or after).

workedExamples.prompt: Take a menu choice from the user and ask again until they choose to exit (it must be asked at least once).

steps.explain: The body runs FIRST, because the condition has not been checked yet.
The user's choice is written to the screen.
Only now is the condition checked: if the choice is not "exit", the body runs again.

exercises.question: What is the main difference between DO-WHILE and WHILE?
options: DO-WHILE checks the condition at the end, so the body runs at least once
There is no difference between them

feedback.correct: Correct. In DO-WHILE the check is at the end, so the body is guaranteed to run once.
feedback.incorrect: The difference is the PLACE where the condition is checked: in DO-WHILE it is at the end, so the body runs at least once.

exercises.question: When choice ← "exit", how many times does a WHILE choice ≠ "exit" loop run?

feedback.correct: Correct. The condition is FALSE from the start, so the WHILE body never runs.
feedback.incorrect: WHILE checks the condition first; "exit" ≠ "exit" is FALSE, so the body never runs.

exercises.question: In the same scenario (choice ← "exit"), how many times does a DO-WHILE loop run?

feedback.correct: Correct. DO-WHILE checks the condition AFTER the body, so the body runs at least once.
feedback.incorrect: By definition, DO-WHILE runs the body first; the condition is checked only after that.

exercises.question: Put the order in which a DO-WHILE loop runs in the correct order.
steps: If the condition is TRUE, go back to the body
If the condition is FALSE, the loop ends

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: A DO-WHILE loop is called a ___-test loop because the condition check is done at the very end.

exercises.question: Which loop is more natural for the scenario "show the menu at least once, then repeat until the user wants to quit"?

feedback.correct: Correct. DO-WHILE is the most natural choice when you need an "at least once" guarantee.
feedback.incorrect: "It must run at least once" is exactly what DO-WHILE guarantees.

summary: DO-WHILE: the body runs first, the condition is checked after (post-test).
WHILE: the condition is checked first (pre-test), and the body may never run.
If you need something to run at least once, prefer DO-WHILE.
